label: late copy-phase steps whose fed-back input is q/x/3/v/d/l/r/b/i (strongest on q)
explanation: About 90% of activation mass falls in the copy phase, and the rate climbs with position: 0 at recall_idx 1, about 2% at recall_idx 2-3, 27-35% at recall_idx 5-8 (to_go 0-1 holds about 70% of mass). Within those late copy steps it is selective for the token being fed back in: q is by far the strongest (39% rate, 37% of mass, and nearly all the top activations are a copy-phase q input), then x, 3, v, d, l, r, b, i. Out_tok, prev_tok, first_tok, digit count and correctness have little effect. A small remainder (about 8% of mass) fires at original step t=2 (often on q, e.g. w q at t=1-2) and rarely elsewhere in the original phase. It almost never fires at t=0, at the delimiter, or at recall_idx 0-1. Precision is limited because even for favored tokens late in the copy phase it fires on only a fraction of steps, and recall is limited by weak firing on other tokens. A token-weighted soft feature rather than a crisp rule.
